standard.title: Design to examine and communicate
standard.description: design and structure media arts works that examine and communicate ideas, perspectives and/or meaning
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can design and structure media arts works using pre-production processes and apply media arts concepts to construct representations for specific audiences. They have applied genre codes and conventions and reflected on communicative intent. They have not yet designed works that specifically examine and communicate ideas — applying critical analysis of existing conventions to produce works that confirm or challenge them.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students design and structure media arts works that examine and communicate ideas, perspectives and/or meaning using pre-production processes and deliberate application of technical and symbolic codes.

nodes.label: Critical analysis of genre conventions
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can analyse how technical and symbolic codes in a specific genre, auteur or film movement communicate values, themes or ideas — and identify how those codes could be used, confirmed or challenged in original work.
nodes.minimum_width: Analyse how technical and symbolic codes in one genre communicate at least two specific values, themes or ideas, and identify how those codes could be replicated or challenged in an original work.
nodes.typical_width: Examine technical and symbolic codes in specific film, television or radio genres; analyse how codes construct stereotypical or alternative representations; identify conventions that confirm or challenge audience expectations; use pre-production processes (shot list, treatment, storyboard) to trial ideas before designing.
wider: Analyse how a specific auteur's use of technical and symbolic codes constructs a recognisable visual/audio language — and design an original work that either pays homage to or deliberately subverts that style, documenting the design decisions

Examine how the same genre conventions have been used differently in film works from different decades or cultural contexts — identifying how social forces shaped the conventions, and designing a response that positions itself in relation to that history
nodes.hinge_reason: Critical analysis of genre conventions is the conceptual prerequisite for designing works that examine ideas — without it, production is replication rather than examination, and the 'examine' command term is not met.

response_modes.reason: Students need a structured analytical framework: 'What values does this code communicate? Who benefits from this representation? What alternative representation would challenge it?' This reasoning chain grounds design decisions in critical analysis.

success_criteria: Student can analyse how at least two technical and symbolic codes in a genre communicate values, themes or ideas
Student can identify how those codes could be used or challenged in original design work

nodes.label: Pre-production design
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use pre-production tools to design and structure a media arts work — making deliberate decisions about how technical and symbolic codes will examine and communicate ideas for an intended audience.
nodes.minimum_width: Produce a pre-production document (shot list, storyboard, shooting script, treatment or screenplay) for a planned media arts work — including at least three design decisions explicitly linked to the ideas, perspectives or meaning to be examined.
nodes.typical_width: Use pre-production processes to design and structure media arts works across two or more forms — documenting how camera work, sound, editing, mise-en-scène or media technologies will construct representations; trial ideas for different production approaches before committing; design alternative representations of the same subject.
wider: Design a media arts work using a storyboard and shooting script — then design an alternative version of the same work that challenges the representations constructed in the first version, comparing how each communicates differently to audiences

Design a social media campaign or community service announcement using detailed pre-production documentation — including target audience analysis, platform selection reasoning, and representation design rationale

response_modes.reason: Pre-production design discipline at Y9-10 requires sustained investment — students who use pre-production tools superficially produce works that are not designed but assembled. Thorough pre-production is the difference between examination and illustration.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The range of pre-production tools and design contexts at Y9-10 (treatment, shooting script, shot list, social media campaign design, documentary design) is genuinely rich — students who work across multiple forms develop much stronger critical design thinking.
success_criteria: Student produces a pre-production document for a planned media arts work
Student can explain at least three design decisions in terms of the ideas, perspectives or meaning to be examined
